passage.title: The Fisherman's Lesson
passage.text:
Mang Isko had fished the same bay for forty years. Every dawn he pushed his small boat into the water and came back by noon with a basket of fish. But this year the baskets were lighter. Some days he came home with almost nothing.

His granddaughter Tess, who was in Grade 4, asked why. "The big boats with the fine nets take everything," he said. "Even the small fish that have not laid eggs yet. So next year there are fewer fish, and the year after, fewer still."

Tess read about this in school. Her teacher called it overfishing. The class wrote letters to the town council asking for a rule to protect the young fish. Tess read hers aloud at the meeting, her voice shaking at first, then growing steady.

The council agreed to set a no-fishing season in the bay for three months each year. Mang Isko grumbled about the lost days. But two years later, his basket was heavy again. "Your letter did that," he told Tess. She shook her head. "The fish did that. We just gave them time."

words.meaning: complained in a low, unhappy voice
words.example: He grumbled about the long line.

words.meaning: a group of people who make decisions for a town
words.example: The council voted to build a new park.

items.prompt: According to Mang Isko, why were there fewer fish each year?
choices: Big boats caught even the young fish before they laid eggs.
He fished too close to shore.
items.why: He explains that the big boats take even the small fish "that have not laid eggs yet," so fewer fish are born.

items.prompt: How long did the council's no-fishing season last each year?
items.why: "A no-fishing season in the bay for three months each year."

items.prompt: "Her voice shaking at first, then growing steady." What does this show about Tess?
choices: She was nervous but became more confident.
She was angry at the council.
items.why: A shaking voice shows nerves; a steady voice shows she gained confidence as she spoke.

items.prompt: Which word means almost the same as grumbled?
items.why: To grumble is to complain in a low, unhappy voice.

choices: Mang Isko fished for forty years and liked to push his boat at dawn.
Fish were disappearing because of overfishing, so Tess and her class asked the council for a rule. The council made a no-fishing season, and the fish came back.
Tess's teacher taught the class a new word.
items.why: This covers the problem, what Tess did, and the result, without small details.

items.prompt: What does overfishing mean in the passage?
choices: Catching more fish than the sea can replace
items.why: The passage links it to taking even the young fish so that "next year there are fewer fish."

items.prompt: Why did Tess say "The fish did that. We just gave them time"?
choices: She did not want credit; the rest came from letting the fish grow.
She thought her letter was bad.
She wanted her grandfather to stop fishing.
items.why: She shook her head at the praise and pointed out that protecting the fish, not her letter alone, fixed the problem.

steps: The class wrote letters to the council.
The council set a no-fishing season.
Mang Isko's basket was heavy again.
items.why: The problem came first, then the letters, then the rule, and the recovery two years later.

items.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Protecting young fish helped the bay recover.
items.why: The story's big point is that giving the fish time to grow brought them back.

items.prompt: At what time of day did Mang Isko push his boat into the water? (one word)
items.why: "Every dawn he pushed his small boat into the water."
